messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: table grob
parts:
Hi,

I'm working on a new version of tableGrob. A prototype is here:
https://gist.github.com/1899720

Now I need to add decorations, row+col headers, support for tables
package, etc. but I think the basic design is sound. How should the
row/column headers (and their justification) work with respect to the
new axis guides in ggplot2? My thinking is that only the core of the
table should be aligned with the plot panel, typically, so I would
specify the table justification relative to the core only. The
optional row and column header(s) would extend from there, on the
sides.

Cheers,

b.

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: table grob
parts:
Hi,

Thanks, Beptiste,

At the moment, first implementation of guide_table is:

d <- ddply(iris, .(Species), colwise(mean))
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Species)) + geom_point() +
scale_y_discrete(guide = guide_table(data = d, position = "left"))

What is most difficult is to handle header.
A header will be place on the top of the table, so it is out of region
of the axis.
This is a kind of special case.

kohske

messages.subject: Re: table grob
parts:
Indeed, multiple headers à la tables::tabular() turn out to be a real
nightmare :(

I got kind of stuck here; it seems my best option is to try again from
scratch using gtable and see if that helps. I've updated the gist, it
looks promising but there are a couple of bugs in gtable (gtable_join,
also compare.units fails with arithmetic units, see my pull request).

Cheers,

b.
